summary: This continuation constructs the geometric circle method for polynomial maps to smooth affine hypersurfaces, with rank-Hankel arc strata, compact-support Fourier complexes, signed configuration-space first pages and monodromy parity. It separates independent dimension, polynomial-counting and prime-choice prefixes from the parent arithmetic estimates. Conservative comparison and irreducibility ranges are distinguished from unproved sharper targets. Explicit infinity-germ obstructions and controlled collars delimit a conditional, rather than unconditional, mapping-space degeneration argument. Independent review replaces the projection audit by a cumulative-degree finite-grid proof and the unread Katz input by the exact accepted Fourier supplier. Four named gaps remain.

declarations.provides: Evaluation of multivariate polynomials through a coefficient ring homomorphism and assigned variables; read declaration at pin.
Natural-valued matrix rank over a field, defined through the associated linear map; not a determinantal scheme.
Existing Hahn-series carrier with integer exponents; coefficient operations suffice for the finite residue expressions.
Valuation at infinity on rational functions: nonzero f/g has exp(deg f−deg g); its completion is already available in the same module.
In a commutative Noetherian ring, a proper ideal has height at most its span rank. The geometric componentwise dimension translation remains GCM.0.
For coprime residue and modulus, there is a prime above any bound in the prescribed class. Read the quantified theorem at the pin.
For distinct odd primes the product of the two Legendre symbols is the usual parity sign; p≡1 mod4 removes it.
For an odd prime p, the Legendre symbol of 2 is the character χ₈(p).
Spectral object in an abelian category with functorial connecting maps and exactness. It is a carrier; a finite localization filtration with its abutment is not supplied by this declaration.
Curries a continuous map X×Y→Z to a continuous map X→C(Y,Z) with the compact-open topology.
A nonempty locally closed subset of a Jacobson space meets the closed points.
A locally finite-type scheme over a Jacobson scheme is Jacobson.
The based fundamental group of the unit additive circle is multiplicatively equivalent to Z, with deck-endpoint convention fixed by the covering construction.

audit.conclusion: The parent audit has finite-Fourier fragments but not geometric arc schemes, compact-support Artin–Schreier complexes, geometric Weyl differencing, monodromy parity or germ mapping-space comparison. This new Part II has no existing audit row; that is not evidence that everything is absent.

nodes.title: Affine dimension theorem for intersections
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, if irreducible closed Y,Z⊂A^M meet, each component C of Y∩Z has dim C≥dim Y+dim Z−M. For a closed V whose every component meets Z, dim(V∩Z)≤0 implies dim V≤M−dim Z. Independently, every component of the nonempty zero locus of r polynomials in A^M has dimension at least M−r.
proofSteps: Use the diagonal in A^M×A^M to express the intersection by M equations in Y×Z.

For each minimal prime P over the ideal of the intersection equations, localize at P. The localized ideal has unique minimal prime P, so Ideal.height_le_spanRank bounds that prime height by the number of equations. Translate back by the catenary dimension formula for finite-type domains; an unlocalized bound on the minimum height of the ideal is insufficient.
For the consequence choose a maximal-dimensional component of V; do not infer nonempty intersection from a dimension inequality.
acceptance: Two coordinate planes in A³ meet in a line and attain the bound.
Disjoint parallel lines do not satisfy the nonempty-intersection hypothesis.
For a cone, justify that every irreducible component contains the vertex before using the diagonal argument.

nodes.title: Degree bound for a finite Cartesian grid
nodes.statement: Let V⊂A^N_K be a nonempty closed algebraic set over any field K. Write V_i for its reduced geometric irreducible components, e_i=dim V_i, Δ_i=deg V_i, e=max_i e_i and Δ=Σ_i Δ_i. For every nonempty finite S⊂K, #(V(K)∩S^N)≤Σ_i Δ_i|S|^(e_i)≤Δ|S|^e. The empty set contributes zero; nilpotents do not change the count. No change of coordinates, field-size restriction or coefficient-height bound is required.
proofSteps: Base change to an algebraic closure and bound the union by the sum over its geometric irreducible components; the components need not descend to K.
Induct on the dimension of one component W. In dimension zero its number of geometric points is at most deg W.

If dim W=e>0, choose a coordinate x_j nonconstant on W. For a∈S, x_j=a does not contain W. Its nonempty section has pure dimension e−1 by the componentwise principal ideal theorem and finite-type dimension formula. The projective closure meets that hyperplane in a projective degree-deg W section with scheme multiplicities; deleting the part at infinity and passing to reduced components gives cumulative degree at most deg W. This is the degree-one case of LR14v2 Theorem 1.1.

Apply the induction hypothesis to each section, viewed in the remaining N−1 coordinates. Sum the disjoint slices over a∈S to obtain deg W·|S|^e, then sum the components. This adapts the affine coordinate-slicing proof of LR14v2 Proposition 2.3 from F_q to an arbitrary finite S.

Only the inequality for affine hyperplane-section degree is used. LR14v2 Lemma 2.6 states an equality that can fail when the projective intersection has points at infinity; E49 records the correction.
acceptance: A coordinate e-plane attains |S|^e with degree one.
A parabola y=x² has degree two but its section x=0 has degree one; an equality for every affine section is unnecessary.
A line together with arbitrarily many isolated points requires cumulative degree, not just the degree of its top-dimensional component.
The hyperbola xy=1 causes no exceptional-projection problem: the proof slices in the original coordinates.

nodes.title: Fibre-dimension strata for geometric Weyl differencing

For e_j≥0, dim φ⁻¹(W_j)=dim W_j+e_j; the pieces with e_j=−∞ have empty inverse image. This is the finite stratification adapter used to maximize base dimension plus fibre cohomological degree in GCM.8.
proofSteps: Import the constructibility of fibre-dimension level sets from SF.0/generic-fibre-spreading(c), whose dimension case is Stacks 05F9. Noetherian quasi-compactness makes these loci constructible, and finite refinement gives irreducible locally closed pieces.
Apply SF.0/fibre-dimension-formula to the finitely many components over each piece. Constant nonempty fibre dimension gives the maximum total dimension dim W_j+e_j; empty fibres are kept separate.
acceptance: The projection of a union of a horizontal and a vertical line has distinct fibre-dimension strata.

nodes.title: Degree-uniform polynomial point bound
nodes.statement: Let V⊂A^N over F_q(T) be nonempty, of dimension e≥0 and geometric cumulative degree Δ. For each integer h≥1, the number of u∈V(F_q[T]) with max_j |u_j|<q^h is at most Δq^(he), where |0|=0 and |a|=q^(deg a) for a≠0. Empty V contributes zero. For h≤0 only the zero vector can occur, and it contributes exactly when it belongs to V. All constants are independent of q and of coefficient heights.
proofSteps: For h≥1 take S={a∈F_q[T]:deg a<h}, including zero, so |S|=q^h.
Apply finite-projection-degree in the original coordinates with the explicit constant Δ; its proof uses no projection or coordinate change.
For h≤0 the strict ball contains only zero. In BV15 the inclusive height bound q^N corresponds to the present h=N+1; the boundary conventions therefore agree.
acceptance: A coordinate affine e-plane has exactly q^(he) points in the strict positive-height box.
At h=0 nonzero constants are excluded; the count is zero or one.
A zero-dimensional variety has at most its degree many rational points regardless of h.

nodes.title: Choose a coefficient prime for fixed odd characteristic
nodes.statement: For each odd prime p and bound B there is a prime ℓ>max(B,p) with ℓ≡−1 mod p; hence ℓ≠p and the order of its residue in F_p× is exactly two. The assertion is independent of f,n,d.
proofSteps: Apply the pinned primes-in-arithmetic-progressions theorem to the unit residue −1 modulo p.
Since p is odd, −1≠1 and (−1)²=1. Enlarge the bound rather than choosing a possibly forbidden prime.
acceptance: For p=5 the residue 4 has order two.
Exclude p=2, where −1 has order one.
The chosen prime exceeds both B and p, so equality of coefficient and residue characteristic cannot occur.

nodes.title: Choose good residue characteristics for fixed coefficient prime
nodes.statement: For a fixed prime ℓ, integers B,k and finite bad-prime set S, there are arbitrarily large primes p>max(B,k,ℓ), p∉S, for which ℓ is a nonsquare modulo p and therefore has even multiplicative order. For odd ℓ choose a nonzero quadratic nonresidue a mod ℓ and the CRT residue p≡a mod ℓ, p≡1 mod4; for ℓ=2 use p≡5 mod8.
proofSteps: Choose the CRT unit class and use Dirichlet above every member of S.
For odd ℓ, quadratic reciprocity has positive sign because p≡1 mod4. For ℓ=2 use the supplementary law.
In a cyclic finite field unit group, an odd-order element is a square; conclude even order.
acceptance: The class 5 mod8 makes 2 a nonsquare.
For odd ℓ, a must be nonzero so the CRT class is a unit.
Avoidance is uniform over any prescribed finite set, not a single ad hoc characteristic.

nodes.title: Polynomial mapping scheme with a fixed leading vector
nodes.statement: Fix a field K, n≥2, k≥3, f∈K[x₁,…,x_n] of degree k, and a nonzero vector x with f₀(x)=0, where f₀ is the degree-k part. For d≥1 put g_j=x_jT^d+Σ_{0≤i<d}a_{i,j}T^i. Mor_{d,x}(A¹,X) is the closed coefficient scheme in A^(dn) cut out by all coefficients of f(g); its top coefficient is already zero, so kd equations suffice. The leading coefficient is f₀(x); prove its vanishing before dropping that equation.
Identify R-points with the prescribed polynomial tuples and retain the representing-scheme structure, including nilpotents.

nodes.title: Smooth projective closure of X and its irreducibility
nodes.statement: Assume X={f=0}⊂A^n is smooth and the degree-k hypersurface Z={f₀=0}⊂P^(n−1) is smooth. The homogenization defines a smooth projective X̄⊂P^n with boundary Z and X=X̄∖Z.
